title: Modi Pens Tribute as L.K. Advani Turns 99 and Enters His 100th Year
excerpt: Prime Minister Narendra Modi marked Lal Krishna Advani's 99th birthday — which falls on Diwali this year — with a signed article praising the BJP co-founder's political acumen, while party leaders held a puja and havan at BJP headquarters in New Delhi.
body:
• Lal Krishna Advani, born November 8, 1927 in Karachi, turned 99 on Sunday and entered his 100th year; his birthday coincides with Diwali this year.
  • Prime Minister Narendra Modi published a signed tribute article and posted on X: "Respected L.K. Advani Ji enters his hundredth year. On this special occasion, my greetings to him."
  • Modi credited Advani with nurturing generations of BJP workers, giving the party a "Nation First" foundation, and — with Atal Bihari Vajpayee — changing the course of Indian politics.
  • The BJP marked the day with a puja and havan at its New Delhi headquarters led by party president Nitin Nabin, who also visited Advani at his residence with senior leaders.

Lal Krishna Advani entered the 100th year of his life on Sunday, November 8 — his 99th birthday — and Prime Minister Narendra Modi marked the occasion with a detailed signed article published in national newspapers and shared on X, praising the Bharatiya Janata Party co-founder's contribution to Indian politics as "everlasting."

"Today, 8th November, is a landmark day. Respected L.K. Advani Ji enters his hundredth year. On this special occasion, my greetings to him," Modi posted. In the article, he noted that Advani's birthday this year coincides with Diwali, "a festival associated with Prabhu Shri Ram and the Diya," and falls in a year that also marks 75 years of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh, the 125th birth anniversary of Syama Prasad Mookerjee and 100 years of the RSS.

"There are very few people whose lives have touched so many different chapters of modern India."

— Narendra Modi, on L.K. Advani

What Modi's tribute said

Modi picked out two defining qualities: "First, his ideological clarity and intellectual sharpness… Second, the manner in which he exposed the pseudo-secularism propounded by a large section of the Indian polity for many years." He wrote that "Advani Ji nurtured generations of Karyakartas and gave the Party a clear foundation rooted in the principle of Nation First," noting that during Advani's presidencies the Congress fell from 400 to below 200 seats in 1989 and the BJP became the single largest party for the first time in 1996.

On Advani's partnership with Atal Bihari Vajpayee, Modi wrote: "History shows that it is rare for two towering political leaders to work together for several decades, cooperating with each other without becoming competitors. Advani Ji and Atal Ji set a remarkable example. Together, they changed the course of Indian politics." He recalled the Emergency as "a watershed moment in Advani Ji's life," the 1990 Somnath-to-Ayodhya Rath Yatra as an "iconic moment," and Advani's tenure as Home Minister, during which, Modi wrote, his "unequivocal stand against terrorism ensured India got a tough anti-terror law." Modi also recalled helping prepare Advani's nomination papers for the 1991 Gandhinagar Lok Sabha campaign and voting for him as a Gandhinagar voter. He closed: "As Advani Ji enters the hundredth year of his life, I pray that he be blessed with good health and that he continues to inspire us all as he has always done."

A life that tracks modern India

Advani was born in Karachi in 1927 and rebuilt his life after Partition in 1947, leaving Sindh, in Modi's words, "without bitterness." He joined the RSS as a swayamsevak in 1942, chaired the Delhi Metropolitan Council in 1967 and entered Parliament in 1970. He was Information and Broadcasting Minister in the Janata government from 1977, co-founded the BJP in 1980, and served three terms as its national president — 1986-1990, 1993-1998 and 2004-2005 — the longest-serving president in the party's history. His 1990 Rath Yatra reshaped national politics; he was Union Home Minister from 1999 to 2004 and Deputy Prime Minister from 2002 to 2004. He was awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honour, in 2024.

How the BJP marked the day

The party organised a puja and havan at its central office in New Delhi on Sunday morning, led by BJP national president Nitin Nabin with senior leaders, followed by a video presentation on Advani's life. Nabin, accompanied by Union Minister Piyush Goyal and general secretary B.L. Santosh, also visited Advani's residence to greet him. "He cultivated a strong cadre of leadership for the BJP, a party that is providing direction to the nation today," Nabin said. "Even today, as we advance on the journey toward a Viksit Bharat, LK Advani's ideas and vision continue to inspire us all." Defence Minister Rajnath Singh posted that "throughout his long public life, Advani ji has set new standards of integrity, dedication and leadership," and Union Minister Nitin Gadkari wrote: "Venerable Advani ji turns 99 today and enters his 100th year. I pray to God for his good health, long life and a life filled with blessings." Advani's daughter Pratibha Advani attended the headquarters event.
